# sherpa-outlet

Where the route's Context is drawn. It is the app's main landmark, and its light DOM IS the Context: on each route change it loads the one app.json names, runs it, and tears the last one down. TRAP T-an-outlet-loads-the-context

## When to use it

Put it in the content of `sherpa-app-shell`: on each route change it loads the Context that `app.json` names and tears the last one down. Settings opens over it, in `<sherpa-dialog data-type="overlay">`, so the Context is not reloaded.

## Example

```html
<sherpa-outlet><h1>Records</h1><p>The Context on screen.</p></sherpa-outlet>
```

| `viewsReady` | `Promise<void>` | read only |  |

## Methods

| Method | What it does |
|---|---|
| `viewsOf(context: string)` | A Context's Views: its own, then the reader's saved ones. |
| `firstView(context: string)` | Its first View, which the URL leaves out. |
| `refreshNav()` | Draw the nav again — after a View is saved or deleted, say. |
| `start(options: OutletOptions)` | Read app.json, load each Context's Views, then open the route's Context. The router's `context` defaults to the app's own. |

## Events

Each one bubbles.

| Event | Detail |
|---|---|
| `context-change` | `{ context: string; view: null \| string }` |
| `context-markup` | `{ context: string; root: this; waitUntil: (work: Promise<unknown>) => undefined }` |
| `context-load` | `{ context: string; view: null \| string }` |
| `settings-open` | `{ page: string }` |
| `settings-close` |  |

## Slots

| Slot | Accepts | What it holds |
|---|---|---|
| (default) | content | the Context's markup, put there by the outlet |
